newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks bounce back, seen erratic.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks bounce back, seen erratic.

text.p: Argentine stocks rebounded Tuesday to close narrowly below their recent five-year high, but the trend remained volatile, dealers said.

"The market took its cue from Wall Street today and bounced back, but a lot of institutional players have moved to the sidelines after last week's options expirations and the purchasing lull could weigh on prices," said Rodrigo Diz at Velox Inversiones.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.3 percent to 825.33, recouping Monday's 1.0 percent loss.
"The bolsa may stall before it aims for new lofty levels, probably in mid-July," Diz said. The MerVal peaked recently at 826.12 and stands 6.1 percent higher so far in June.
Traders said political tension over the affairs of postal magnate Alfredo Yabran, which prompted the justice minister to tender his resignation Tuesday, had not affected trading.

"Really that whole issue does not change market fundamentals, which are strong economic data and rising real investments," another trader said. "However, if we see a bout of profit-taking, players may blame it on politics so that they can push prices lower and bet on losses."
Floor volume recovered to 34.1 million pesos from 22 million Monday, while over-the-counter deals eased to 82.8 million pesos from 88.1 million Monday.
The broad market rose 1.0 percent, with winners lashing losers 43 to 11 and 20 stocks closing unchanged.

The best main-tier performer was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which jumped 9.9 percent on technical buying but was expected to slump again, dealers said. Celulosa dived a similar amount Monday and erased gains of 15 percent to close flat Friday, when buyout rumors were denied. Previously last week it had surged 27 percent.
Other top MerVal risers were construction stock Polledo, which shot up 6.7 percent, and steelmakers Acindar and Siderca, up 2.9 percent and 2.7 percent, respectively.
The only blue-chip losers were carmaker Ciadea, which fell 1.1 percent, Banco de Galicia, down 0.7 percent, and Banco Frances and holding company Garovaglio, both off 0.2 percent.
